QuestionStmt.S: The third element in the second row of adjoint of a matrix $A = [a_{ij}]_{3 \times 3}$ (where $a_{ij} = 2i + j$) is

Solution.S:
Given $a_{ij} = 2i + j$, we form the matrix:

$$A = \begin{bmatrix}
3 & 4 & 5 \\
5 & 6 & 7 \\
7 & 8 & 9
\end{bmatrix}$$

The third element in the second row of adjoint $A$ is the cofactor $C_{23}$ (since adjoint is transpose of cofactor matrix, the element at (2,3) of adjoint is $C_{32}$? Wait: The adjoint of A is the transpose of the cofactor matrix. The element at row 2, column 3 of adj(A) is $C_{32}$ (cofactor of element a_{32}).

But the question says "third element in the second row" — that is element (2,3) of adj(A). That is $C_{32}$.

$C_{32} = (-1)^{3+2} \begin{vmatrix} a_{11} & a_{13} \\ a_{21} & a_{23} \end{vmatrix}$

$a_{11}=3, a_{13}=5, a_{21}=5, a_{23}=7$.

$$C_{32} = (-1)^5 \begin{vmatrix} 3 & 5 \\ 5 & 7 \end{vmatrix} = - (3 \times 7 - 5 \times 5) = - (21 - 25) = -(-4) = 4$$

So the value is $4$.

Final Answer: $$\boxed{4}$$

Hence, the correct option is C.
